annotation.authors_or_issuer: Bulgaria, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, and Sweden (submitted to CCW GGE on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (CCW/GGE.1/2025/WP.4)
annotation.summary_en: Working paper by eleven European states to the CCW GGE on lethal autonomous weapons, arguing that "context-appropriate human judgement and control" is the key concept for ensuring IHL compliance across the weapon system lifecycle, without requiring direct continuous human oversight, and urging consensus language by 2026.
key_provisions_or_claims: Frames the issue as human-machine interaction with context-appropriate human judgement and control to comply with IHL.
Human judgement and control apply across lifecycle: design, legal review (Art. 36 AP I), testing, deployment limits.
Direct or continuous human oversight is not required by IHL; control over parameters before deployment can suffice.
Control includes approval of mission changes, safety stop ability, and adequate operator situational awareness.
Calls on GGE members to turn convergence into concrete language before the 2026 mandate ends.
